1.summary: John proclaims the Word of life, which he heard, saw and touched, so readers can share fellowship with the Father and the Son; God is light, and walking in the light means honestly confessing sin, which God faithfully forgives.
1.lookfor: Notice the senses in the first verse, and the three "if we say" claims.

insights.title: From the beginning
insights.body: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, seen and touched, concerning the Word of life (1:1). It echoes the opening of John's Gospel: in the beginning was the Word.

insights.title: Touched with our hands
insights.body: The writer stresses physical senses, hearing, seeing, touching (1:1), against teachers who denied that Christ truly came in a body.

insights.title: Fellowship
insights.body: We proclaim this so you may have fellowship, koinonia, with us, and our fellowship is with the Father and his Son (1:3). Shared life with God and his people.

insights.title: God is light
insights.body: God is light, and in him is no darkness at all (1:5). Light means truth, purity and openness; you can't claim fellowship with God while walking in darkness.

insights.title: If we say
insights.body: Three false claims: if we say we have fellowship but walk in darkness, if we say we have no sin, if we say we haven't sinned (1:6-10). Each is a form of self-deception.

insights.title: Faithful to forgive
insights.body: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness (1:9). Forgiveness rests on God's faithfulness to his covenant.

insights.title: Walking in the light
insights.body: John says honesty about sin is the way into fellowship, not out of it. What do you need to bring into the light?

2.summary: John writes so readers won't sin, but if they do, Jesus is their advocate and atoning sacrifice; knowing God shows in keeping his commands and loving others; he encourages children, fathers and young men, warns against loving the world, and identifies antichrists who left the church and deny the Son.
2.lookfor: Notice the repeated phrase "by this we know," and the description of those who went out.

insights.title: An advocate
insights.body: If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous (2:1). The word paraklētos is a legal helper who speaks for you; Jesus used it of the Spirit.

insights.title: Atoning sacrifice
insights.body: He is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only ours but the whole world's (2:2). The word is the same as the mercy seat language Paul uses.

insights.title: A new old command
insights.body: The command to love isn't new, it's the old one you had from the beginning; yet it is new, because the darkness is passing and the true light already shines (2:7-8).

insights.title: Children, fathers, young men
insights.body: John addresses little children, fathers and young men (2:12-14). These may be stages of age or of spiritual maturity, or simply ways to address the whole church warmly.

insights.title: Don't love the world
insights.body: Don't love the world or the things in it: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life (2:15-16). The world here means human life organized without God, and it is passing away (2:17).

insights.title: Antichrist
insights.body: Many antichrists have come (2:18). The word appears only in John's letters, for anyone who denies that Jesus is the Christ, opposing and replacing him.

insights.title: They went out from us
insights.body: They went out from us, but they weren't of us (2:19). The split was painful; John reassures those who stayed that they have the anointing and know the truth (2:20).

insights.title: What you love
insights.body: John contrasts loving the world with doing God's will. What is competing for your heart's affection right now?

3.summary: See what great love the Father has given us, that we are called God's children, and when Christ appears we will be like him; children of God don't keep on sinning; love one another, not like Cain, but as Christ laid down his life, in deed and truth, and if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts.
3.lookfor: Notice the contrast between Cain and Christ, and the comfort in verse 20.

names.name: Cain
names.gloss: Adam's son, who murdered his brother Abel.

insights.title: Children of God
insights.body: Behold what manner of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God, and so we are (3:1). The last phrase insists it's reality, not just a title.

insights.title: We will be like him
insights.body: What we will be hasn't yet appeared, but when he appears we will be like him, because we'll see him as he is (3:2).

insights.title: Doesn't keep on sinning
insights.body: Whoever is born of God doesn't practice sin (3:9). Since John also said we deceive ourselves if we claim no sin (1:8), he means a settled pattern of life, not occasional failure.

insights.title: Not like Cain
insights.body: Don't be like Cain, who was of the evil one and murdered his brother because his own deeds were evil and his brother's righteous (3:12).

insights.title: Hate is murder
insights.body: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer (3:15), as Jesus taught that anger is the root of murder.

insights.title: In deed and truth
insights.body: By this we know love, that he laid down his life for us; we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers (3:16). Love not in word or speech but in deed and truth (3:18).

insights.title: Greater than our hearts
insights.body: If our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and knows all things (3:20). An anxious conscience isn't the final judge; God is, and he is merciful.

insights.title: Love in action
insights.body: John says love that sees a need and does nothing isn't God's love. What need around you could your love meet this week?

4.summary: John urges testing the spirits, since every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ came in the flesh is from God; love comes from God, for God is love, shown in sending his Son as an atoning sacrifice; perfect love casts out fear, and whoever loves God must love his brother.
4.lookfor: Notice how often the word love appears, and how John defines it by what God did.

insights.title: Test the spirits
insights.body: Don't believe every spirit, but test them, because many false prophets have gone out (4:1). The test is the incarnation: confessing that Jesus Christ came in the flesh (4:2).

insights.title: Greater is he
insights.body: Greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world (4:4). The believer's security doesn't depend on the strength of opposition.

insights.title: God is love
insights.body: God is love (4:8, 4:16). Not just that God loves, but that love is his very nature. Twice John says it, the only place the Bible states it so directly.

insights.title: Not that we loved God
insights.body: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins (4:10). Love is defined by God's action, not our feelings.

insights.title: No one has seen God
insights.body: No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God remains in us (4:12). The invisible God becomes visible in a loving community.

insights.title: Fear and punishment
insights.body: There is no fear in love; perfect love casts out fear, because fear has to do with punishment (4:18). In a culture fearful of gods and fate, this was freeing news.

insights.title: Love God, love brother
insights.body: Whoever says he loves God but hates his brother is a liar, for he can't love God whom he hasn't seen if he doesn't love his brother whom he has (4:20). The two great commands are joined.

insights.title: Fear and love
insights.body: John says perfect love drives out fear. What fear in your relationship with God might his love be ready to drive out?

5.summary: Whoever believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God and overcomes the world; God's testimony through water, blood and Spirit is that eternal life is in his Son; John writes so believers may know they have eternal life, can pray with confidence, and should keep themselves from idols.
5.lookfor: Notice the word know repeated near the end, and the abrupt final sentence.

insights.title: Not burdensome
insights.body: His commands aren't burdensome (5:3). For one born of God, obeying is not grinding duty but family likeness.

insights.title: Faith overcomes
insights.body: This is the victory that overcomes the world, our faith (5:4). Jesus said, take heart, I have overcome the world.

insights.title: Water and blood
insights.body: He came by water and blood, not by water only (5:6). Some taught that the divine Christ came on Jesus at his baptism but left before the cross. John insists the same Jesus was baptized and died.

insights.title: That you may know
insights.body: I write these things so that you may know you have eternal life (5:13). John's Gospel was written so you might believe (John 20:31); this letter so believers might be sure.

insights.title: Confidence in prayer
insights.body: If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us (5:14). Prayer aligns us with his will, and we can trust he listens.

insights.title: Keep yourselves from idols
insights.body: The letter ends abruptly: little children, keep yourselves from idols (5:21). An idol is anything put in God's place, including a false picture of Jesus.

insights.title: The true God
insights.body: We are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ; this is the true God and eternal life (5:20). The letter closes where John's Gospel opened: Jesus is God.

insights.title: Assurance
insights.body: John wrote so believers could know, not just hope, they have eternal life. What makes you doubt, and what in this letter answers it?

intro.who: The writer doesn't name himself but claims to be an eyewitness who heard, saw and touched the Word of life (1:1). Tradition names the apostle John; its language closely resembles John's Gospel. Some scholars think it came from John's circle of disciples.
intro.when: About AD 85–100, probably from Ephesus, after John's Gospel.
intro.why: A group had left the church, denying that Jesus Christ came in the flesh and claiming to be without sin (2:19, 4:2). John writes to reassure those who stayed that they truly know God, giving tests of genuine faith: believing in Jesus, obeying God's commands and loving one another.

outline.title: Children of God love one another
Test the spirits; God is love
Faith that overcomes; assurance of life
